highlights.text: Bihar and Jharkhand must pay Rs 1 lakh each, with interest, to daily-wage workers in a 25-year-old dues case.

highlights.caseName: In Re: Recent Rape Incidents in Delhi NCR
highlights.text: Delhi-NCR police must map unsafe spots and audit lighting and CCTV within four weeks.

highlights.caseName: Puneet Batra v. Union of India
highlights.text: Stay on a Delhi HC ruling that upheld a GST search of an advocate's office.

highlights.caseName: In Re Exorbitant Pricing of Life Saving Patented Medicines
highlights.text: The Centre can invoke Section 100 of the Patents Act to supply unaffordable life-saving drugs.

items.caseName: Bihar State Ardh Sarkari Arajpati Karamchari Maha Sangh v. State of Bihar
items.headline: Rs 1 lakh each for daily-wagers in 25-year-old Bihar dues case
items.text: Bihar and Jharkhand must pay each daily-wage worker Rs 1 lakh, with 12% interest on delayed PF and 6% on delayed wages. The Court rejected a flat Rs 42.50-a-day rate as unfair.
items.why: Workers not yet traced get 12 months to claim, and verified lists must go online within 4 weeks.

items.caseName: In Re: Recent Rape Incidents in Delhi NCR
items.coram: J.B. Pardiwala, K. Vinod Chandran, JJ.
items.headline: Safety audit of Delhi-NCR public spaces ordered within 4 weeks
items.text: In the suo motu case, police must map vulnerable spots district by district, step up patrols and audit street lighting and CCTV, including at transit hubs. Status reports are due in four weeks.
items.why: The bench described the incidents as a systemic failure of policing and administration.

items.caseName: Owners and Parties Interested in M.V. Nereus Progress v. Om Freight Forwarders Ltd.
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Joymalya Bagchi, V. Mohana, JJ.
items.headline: Bareboat charter ends on a valid termination notice
items.text: A BARECON 2017 bareboat charter ends once a valid termination notice is served, without repossession; the former charterer then holds the ship only as a bailee. The sister-vessel arrest was vacated.

items.caseName: State of Maharashtra v. Ramesh Sukrya Mhatre
items.headline: Bail of Shiv Sena corporator in doctors' assault case cancelled
items.text: The Court set aside the Bombay High Court's bail order and told Mhatre to surrender within three days. It said a firm message was needed that doctors cannot be attacked.

items.caseName: Puneet Batra v. Union of India
items.headline: Delhi HC ruling upholding GST search of advocate's office stayed
items.text: The Court stayed the High Court judgment and gave the respondents three weeks to reply. The bench asked why the reasons for searching a lawyer's office were not disclosed.

items.caseName: Rubabuddin Shaikh v. Central Bureau of Investigation
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Joymalya Bagchi, V. Mohana, JJ.
items.headline: Notice on challenge to acquittal of 22 in Sohrabuddin encounter case
items.text: Notice was issued on the appeal against the Bombay High Court's acquittal of 22 accused. The bench called 92 hostile witnesses a serious concern but said the discharge of Amit Shah will not be reopened.

items.caseName: Mamata Banerjee v. Election Commission of India
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Joymalya Bagchi, V. Mohana, JJ.
items.headline: ECI to decide Trinamool name and symbol dispute within 3 months
items.text: Both sides must file affidavits within four weeks. The Election Commission must then decide the TMC symbol dispute within three months.

items.caseName: Anjan Datta v. Union of India
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Joymalya Bagchi, V. Mohana, JJ.
items.headline: No stay on MDR charge for UPI payments above Rs 2,000
items.text: The Court declined to stay the merchant discount rate on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000. The Centre must file an affidavit explaining the legal and technical basis for the levy.

items.caseName: Fanindra Das v. The General Manager
items.headline: Electricity is part of the right to life: Railways told to give connection
items.text: Calling electricity indispensable to life under Article 21, the Court quashed the 2011 and 2012 refusals. North Eastern Railway must provide the connection within 30 days.

items.caseName: Indian Secular Front v. Election Commission of India
items.headline: Order reserved on ISF plea over 'Envelope' symbol in Nandigram by-poll
items.text: The judge questioned whether the ECI was guided by a private party in allotting ISF's symbol to the TMC-Democratic faction. The ECI said the plea was meant to derail the poll.

items.caseName: Manoj Chaudhary v. State (NCT of Delhi)
items.headline: Re-arrest needs a magistrate's reasoned permission after a vitiated arrest
items.text: Where an accused is freed because grounds of arrest were not supplied, police need a magistrate's reasoned permission to re-arrest. Re-arrest merely because charges were added was illegal.
items.why: Lays down the procedure after an Article 22(1) violation.

items.caseName: Ms G v. State (NCT of Delhi)
items.headline: Rape survivor must be heard before the accused gets bail
items.text: A victim may take part at every stage, including regular bail hearings. The bail order passed without notice to her was set aside and sent back for a fresh hearing within two weeks.

items.caseName: Ayush Kumar v. National Testing Agency
items.headline: NTA to issue duplicate NEET-UG scorecards to foreign medical graduates
items.text: The Court relaxed document requirements, allowing self-attested affidavits and photographs. Applications are due within 7 days and scorecards within 7 more, ahead of the FMGE.

items.caseName: Janhvi Kapoor v. John Does
items.headline: Amici appointed to settle scope of celebrity personality rights
items.text: The Court picked three suits to decide whether using a celebrity's photo breaches personality rights when the photographer owns the copyright. Gautam Bhatia and Rohan Alva were appointed amici.

items.caseName: Tabinda Nazir v. Union Territory
items.headline: Baramulla fake-decree probe moved to Crime Branch SIT
items.text: The Court transferred the probe into allegedly fabricated judicial records to the Crime Branch and formed an SIT. Advocate Tabinda Nazir was granted interim bail.

items.caseName: Dr. Ashwin Hebbar K. v. State of Karnataka
items.headline: Internal Committee report cannot close a sexual harassment FIR
items.text: An offence under Section 354A IPC is cognizable and needs a police probe, so an Internal Committee's closure does not end it. Delay in filing is a trial defence, not a ground to quash.

items.caseName: Pratap N.M. v. State of Karnataka
items.headline: FIR against YouTuber over sodium-in-water experiment quashed
items.text: Sodium is not an explosive substance and the video showed no malicious intent under the Explosive Substances Act. The FIR was quashed with a caution against repeating such stunts.

items.caseName: In Re Exorbitant Pricing of Life Saving Patented Medicines
items.headline: Centre can use Section 100 Patents Act to supply costly patented drugs
items.text: Section 100 of the Patents Act lets the Centre make and supply patented medicines for non-commercial government use. The Court said this is warranted where life-saving drugs are priced out of reach.
items.why: Opens a route to affordable access to high-priced life-saving medicines.

items.caseName: Muhammed Nihad v. State of Kerala
items.headline: Anticipatory bail for YouTuber 'Thoppi' in obscenity case
items.text: After viewing the video, the Court found no obscene or sexually coloured words spoken by the applicant against the complainant. Custodial interrogation was unnecessary, so bail was granted.

items.caseName: K.R. Periyakaruppan v. R. Seenivasa Sethupathi
items.headline: Challenge to one-vote win in Tirupattur rejected at threshold
items.text: The election petition was rejected for not pleading material facts. Even taken as true, the allegations did not show the result was materially affected.

items.caseName: R v. R
items.headline: Not every clash between wife and in-laws is cruelty
items.text: The Madurai Bench refused the husband a divorce, finding no grave or continuing cruelty. The wife living with her parents while he worked abroad was not desertion.

items.caseName: Women Wrestlers v. Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh
items.court: Rouse Avenue Court, New Delhi, Delhi
items.headline: Notice to Brij Bhushan on wrestlers' appeal against his acquittal
items.text: The court sought responses from Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and co-accused Vinod Tomar on four women wrestlers' appeal against their acquittal. The matter is next listed on 9 October.
